description: About Us At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets. We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand. We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel. Read more about what we’re building here . About the role Solutions Engineers at Axle build the integrations and technical infrastructure that enable our customers to connect distributed energy devices, orchestrate them, and participate in electricity markets. This is a generalist engineering role, encompassing core software engineering, customer implementation, and solution design. You will work closely with our customers to understand their technical requirements, build integrations, solve complex technical challenges, and help shape our product based on real world feedback. We encourage engineers to own as much of the problem space as they can. You will spend time talking to customers, getting feedback from users, and working closely with market operators, while collaborating with Product to deliver scalable engineering solutions. At Axle, we work in a deliberately flat structure. That means fewer layers, faster decisions, and more ownership for everyone. Solutions Engineering at Axle looks like Forming a deep understanding of our domain, our platform, and our customers' technical challenges, so you have enough context to execute at speed. Building and maintaining integrations with customer systems, distributed energy devices, and third-party platforms. Working closely with customers to troubleshoot technical issues, support implementations, and design scalable solutions. Build tailored demos and proofs of concept using Formance’s APIs and tooling. Guide technical evaluations, investigate questions, and help prospects assess product fit. Ability to partner effectively with developers and influence secure design decisions. Familiarity with GitHub-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines. Nice to Have Development experience with Ruby on Rails or similar dynamic languages. Knowledge of AWS ECS/EKS, container security, secrets management and infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation, Terraform). Experience building or maturing an AppSec program from early stages. SOAR Automation & Scripting experience. Experience working in a PCI-compliant environment working with annual reporting needs. description: ***Note:** Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.* ## 🚀 Our Story Partly's mission is to connect the world's parts and we're doing that by building the first global platform for replacement parts, starting with auto parts. Our big vision is to accelerate the world towards a sustainable future where waste is eliminated and all replacement parts are universally searchable, accessible and available to all. Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we utilise bleeding-edge technology to solve challenging but exciting problems that make a huge impact in a $1.9 trillion industry. We've more than tripled our team over the last 12 months and expect to double in size again over the coming 12 months. We're a global team spanning both Europe and Australasia. We provide a scalable digital infrastructure solution to some of the world's largest businesses and the most exciting startups. Partly's solutions are integrated across hundreds of companies globally, providing the backbone for cataloguing and managing parts online. Our investors in Blackbird Ventures (Canva, CultureAmp etc.), Square Peg, Octopus Ventures, Icehouse, Peter Beck (Rocket Lab), Akshay Kothari (Notion Co-Founder) and Dylan Field (Figma Co-Founder). We're continuing to build a world-class team and ensuring Partly is a place where people can do the best work of their lives. We're proud of the culture we've built at Partly, and our [values](https://www.partly.com/careers) are lived throughout every experience. ## 🖍️ This role This is a forward-deployed solutions role at the front line of Partly's European expansion. You'll be the technical engine behind new-market deals across the UK and the Nordics, turning messy real-world problems into signed pilots and putting genuinely differentiated AI in front of the people who run the repair industry. Here's what you'd be working with. Partly runs two connected layers. [Partly.com](http://Partly.com) is the infrastructure platform, the B2B layer that powers parts data, cataloging, and procurement across hundreds of integrations globally. [Partly.ai](http://Partly.ai) is the AI tool for repairers, built on top of that infrastructure, that makes finding and sourcing the right part feel like magic. Both are powered by Interpreter, Partly's proprietary foundation model for understanding automotive parts at scale, trained on licensed OEM build data across 52+ manufacturer agreements and continuously sharpened by feedback from thousands of users across our global network. No general-purpose AI model comes close on parts accuracy, and that is what makes agentic procurement automation possible at the precision the repair industry demands. Your job is to deploy that into markets we haven't cracked yet. Automotive data is scattered around the world in complex, inconsistent formats, and the interesting work is in unifying it into something that drives a customer's business. You'll sit between Sales, Product, and Engineering, resolving the technical blockers that stand between a prospect and a deal, building demos and experimental features that show off what Interpreter can do, and shaping how the product gets built for and applied to each new market. Why join now: Partly closed a $50M Series B at a $500M valuation and is scaling fast across the UK, Europe, the U.S., and Australasia, in a $1.9 trillion industry that has barely been touched by modern software. You'd be early, close to the founders and the model, and given real ownership from day one. If you like ambiguity, owning a problem end to end, and being the person who makes a deal technically possible with frontier AI, this role is built for you. ## 💻 What will you do - **Unblock new-market deals end to end.** Own the technical path from first conversation to signed pilot across the UK and the Nordics: scope integrations, map end-to-end estimating and parts workflows, and clear whatever stands between a prospect and a yes. - **Build integrations that make pilots possible.** Stand up and debug the connections customers depend on (**for example, the CABAS estimating integration for the Nordic customer pilots or quick custom interfaces for client-facing demos**), working close to the data and the code to get them live in test and beyond. - **Build demos and experimental features.** Create market demos and portal prototypes that prove what Partly can do before committing core engineering, iterating fast on what prospects react to. - **Run Technical Readiness Assessments.** Produce the TRAs that map a customer's systems and dependencies so both sides know exactly what a pilot requires. - **Turn data into a commercial case.** Build value proposition frameworks, calculators, and reporting (for example, insurer reporting dashboards) that show customers the value in their own numbers. - **Be the voice of the UK and Nordics customer to Product.** Translate recurring deal blockers into clear, prioritized product asks, and shape how the product gets built and applied for each new market. - **Work cross-functionally to hit deadlines.** Coordinate across Sales, Product, and Engineering to solve customer problems and keep deals moving. Want to learn more about the problems we're solving and the culture we're building at Partly? Hear directly from our team here: [https://shorturl.at/iAFUX](https://shorturl.at/iAFUX) ## 🥷 Your skills - **Comfortable working close to data and code.** You can write SQL, read and debug your way around a codebase, and stand up demos or prototypes yourself rather than waiting on Engineering. - **Strong technical problem solver and systems thinker.** You break ambiguous, messy problems into root causes and generalizable solutions, not one-off fixes. - **Commercially minded.** You understand how a technical decision affects a deal, and you can build the business case (frameworks, calculators, reporting) that moves a customer. - **Excellent communicator who builds rapport.** You hold your own with customers and translate fluently between their world and Partly's Product and Engineering teams. - **Self-directed and high ownership.** You're comfortable being the only solutions person in a market, owning problems end to end with little hand-holding. - **(Preferred)** Experience in a solutions engineering, forward-deployed, or technical pre-sales role, ideally integrating into or selling to enterprise customers. - **(Bonus)** Experience in the automotive, parts, insurance, estimating space, or experience building integrations against messy external data formats. Please note: If you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional. ## 🪅 Benefits - **Competitive base salary + equity.** We offer competitive salaries and generous equity options for all full-time employees, ensuring everyone shares in the financial upside when we win. - **Annual global offsite in New Zealand.** Travel with the rest of the UK and EU team as we gather and connect for 1–2 weeks at our product and engineering hub in Christchurch. - **Parental leave.** Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return to work (four days at full pay for your first three months back). - **Team lunches.** Lunch is provided daily (Monday through Friday) in the office. - **Flexible working hours.** We have flexible working hours and default to working from the office. - **Season openers & events.** We host regular events, including quarterly "season openers" for our UK/EU team, monthly team catch-ups, and weekly happy hours. - **Healthy body, healthy mind.** Every team member gets a £750 annual wellness allowance on a Partly-branded card. Use it for gym memberships, rock climbing, physio, massage, GP visits, prescriptions—anything you or your family need.

description: Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale. We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does. Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place. Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published. Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you. 1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against. 2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on. 3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not. 4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough. Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster. A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job. If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold. 1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus. 2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer. 3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome. You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter. 4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus. Why us? Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate. No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title. We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one. Real ownership. We’re passionate about pioneering an industry, embracing challenges with open arms, and delivering value to the experiences industry. **FareHarbor Core Values:** - Think Client First - We Are One ‘Ohana - Be Curious and Learn - Own It. - Act With Integrity - Embrace the Challenge **Why FareHarbor?** Founding FareHarbor required unwavering passion. Turning a start-up into the world’s leading and largest reservation software for tours, activities, and attractions required relentless dedication and vision. To date, we’ve helped over 20,000 global businesses operate successfully and are proud to have played a role in enabling business owners to live their dreams. And since day one, we’ve known that our real success lies in our people—the Ohana. With each new feature launched and new client onboarded, there is a team of incredible people behind the scenes who are full of dedication, passion, energy, and the will to succeed. We encourage everyone to bring their whole selves to work—to believe in their abilities, to freely express their creativity, and to contribute with their own uniqueness by wearing their true colors. We take care of one another and always prioritize health and wellbeing. We give our people the space and trust to learn, to try, to succeed, to collaborate, to think outside of the box, to make mistakes, and even to fail. And then we come together to try again. From the minute you join, you have a voice. You find your space. You make an impact. We celebrate our victories, shout our successes, and are always eager to tackle new challenges. And we can’t wait to see all that’s to come. ### **About the Role** FareHarbor is looking for a full time **Application Security Engineer** to join our Security Engineering team in Amsterdam. This role will primarily focus on application security and secure SDLC initiatives, while also supporting security monitoring efforts. We are looking for someone who can work closely with our Senior Application Security Engineer on application security reviews, secure development practices, CI/CD security controls, application vulnerability remediation, and broader security engineering initiatives. The ideal candidate is comfortable operating across multiple areas of security, with strong application security expertise and the ability to contribute to automation, detection engineering, and incident response. ### **What you will do:** - Work closely with product, platform, and security teams to ensure security is an integral part of our SDLC - Perform application security reviews, code reviews, threat modeling, and design reviews for new and existing features, promote application security practices across engineering teams - Identify, assess, and help remediate vulnerabilities in applications, APIs, services, and GitLab CI/CD pipelines by implementing and maintaining application security controls such as security policies, SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning, and other CI/CD security controls - Support assessment and remediation such as for penetration test findings, bug bounty findings, vulnerability scan results, internal or external audit by providing technical input, documentation, and evidence - Write and maintain code and automation to support application security workflows, security tooling, vulnerability management, detection, and CI/CD security controls. - Work with engineering teams to provide guidance on secure coding practices, application architecture, authentication, authorization, API security, secrets management, and secure deployment patterns - Support security initiatives, such as IAM, AWS WAF, Help fine-tune security monitoring and detection capabilities, including Elastic SIEM rules, WAF policies, alerting logic, logging improvements, and security automation - Participate in security alert triage, investigation, and incident response activities when needed - Participate in the security on-call rotation ### **Required Skills and Experience:** #### **Technical skills:** - Senior engineer with strong experience in application security, secure SDLC, strong technical knowledge of web/API security, common vulnerabilities, and practical mitigation strategies for OWASP Top 10. - Proven experience performing application security reviews, including code reviews, design reviews, and threat modeling, as well as supporting the remediation of security findings from penetration tests, vulnerability scans, and security audits. - Experience implementing security controls in GitLab CI/CD pipeline, such as SAST, DAST, SCA, secret scanning, IaC scanning, dependency scanning etc. - Strong hands-on programming experience in Python or another high-level language such as Go or Java, with the ability to independently write, review, debug, and maintain code - Good understanding of AWS security concepts, including IAM, WAF, Kubernetes, containers, and infrastructure as code - Experience with security monitoring, alert tuning, SIEM use cases, logging, detection engineering, or WAF rule tuning - Pentesting experience is a plus - Ability to assess risk, prioritize vulnerabilities, and balance security requirements with business needs and engineering realities - Familiarity with security and compliance frameworks such as NIST, PCI DSS, GDPR, SOC 2, SOX, or similar - Good understanding of incident response, security investigations, and technical incident management - Experience with API security, microservices security, and distributed application architectures - Experience with AI-assisted security automation for AppSec triage, vulnerability assessment, detection tuning, and security monitoring workflows using tools such as Cursor, Tines, Elastic, or similar. #### **Soft skills:** - Strong communication skills, able to explain technical security risks clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders - Able to work effectively with product, engineering, platform, infrastructure, and security teams - Proactive attitude, always on the look-out for improving your and our way of working - Strong problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex systems and make decisions based on risk, data, and best practices - Strong relationship building skills across diverse cross-functional teams - Comfortable operating independently and taking ownership of security initiatives from discovery through implementation - Able to provide practical security guidance that enables teams to move quickly and securely ### **Nice to Haves:** - Security certifications such as OSCP, OSWE, OSWA, GWAPT, GWEB, CISSP, CCSP, Security+, AWS Certified Security Specialty, or similar - Experience with bug bounty programs and coordinating vulnerability remediation with third party - Experience with Terraform, infrastructure as code, configuration management, and policy-as-code frameworks - Experience building internal security tooling or developer-facing security automation - Contributions to the security community through research, blog posts, conference talks, open-source tools, or responsible disclosures *This role is available to candidates located in the Netherlands and requires ability to work in a hybrid setup with in-office presence..* ### **Benefits** - Global leave benefit - 22 weeks paid parental leave - 2 weeks paid grandparent leave - Extended care and bereavement leave - Life insurance policy - Pension Plan - Central Amsterdam Location - Discount CZ insurance - Working in a multicultural environment - 45 different nationalities - Commuting allowance for public transport & subsidized lunch - Wellness benefits (Headspace subscription & wellness webinars) - Hybrid friendly - Work-from-home assistance - Educational Opportunities - Individual skill development & growth programming - Social hours & events and team-building - 26 vacation days per year *FareHarbor is committed to creating a diverse environment, and we are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or veteran status. We welcome talent that can offer us new insights and perspectives on challenges that we face, and we take measures to eliminate unconscious bias throughout the interview and hiring process. In tandem, we work to cultivate an inclusive culture in which all of our employees can be their authentic selves.* To learn more about how we use your information, see our [Privacy Statement for Applicants](https://fareharbor.com/legal/privacy-statement-for-applicants/). description: ### What is Nanzen Nanzen is disrupting B2B by bringing agentic workflows to finance operations, automating critical, trust-sensitive flows that still run on emails, spreadsheets, old databases, manual approval chains and basic wire transfers. We are ambitious, we are building Nanzen to be an era-defining company, where there's a clear before and after in B2B commerce. ### The Nanzen team Nanzen's philosophy is to bring the smallest team of the greatest people that cover maximum footprint. We prefer in person but we do hybrid. Life can be better if you can make the best of both worlds. The days we are not sitting next to each other we miss the speed of a whiteboarding session and the good vibes. You need to have the ambition to work on something small that can change the world. This requires your attention and love. It's about caring, not sucking your life into non-existence. We have families and we intend for our kids to see their parents but this is not a 9 to 5 job at Dunder-Mifflin. Trust is everything. At Nanzen we base our relationship on transparency, autonomy and accountability (= allergic to BS). ### The Fintech Engineer role Finance runs on other people's systems. Every one of them has its own format, its own idea of what a transaction is, and its own way of being partially wrong. Making that coherent is most of the work, and it's the part that decides whether anything built on top can be trusted. The architectural bet is that **the model outlives the integrations**. Providers get swapped, companies pivot, a market turns out to work differently than the documentation claimed. What has to survive all of that is one coherent representation that every external system maps into so that adding a country, a partner or a customer is an adapter, not a rewrite of everything above it. #### What you own **The model**. The representation of what two companies agreed and what actually happened between them, and the discipline that keeps it correct as it grows: auditable, idempotent, reconciling to the cent, and reconstructable years later. **The boundary where a decision becomes money**. Nanzen builds agents that take real finance actions, at a volume and granularity no team does by hand. That only works if the layer beneath them is exact. You own that boundary, and you'll shape it alongside the people building the agents. **Reconciliation as a product surface, not a batch job**. Matching, cash application, exceptions, short payments, credits, and specifically what happens to the things that don't match, which is where every finance team actually loses its afternoons. **Bank connectivity, Open Banking and payment initiation**. Instructing payments through bank connectivity and partner providers, the consent and authority models behind them, and reading status and statements back so we know what actually settled. **The substrate the next decade runs on**. E-invoicing networks and standards (Peppol, EN 16931, the national clearance platforms, ISO 20022 across initiation, reporting and remittance) are turning money movement between companies into something structured and machine-readable. That's the blueprint for a better way of paying, and working fluently in it is a large part of this role. **ERP and system-of-record integration**. Pulling orders, invoices, receipts, payments and credits out of ERPs, CRMs and accounting systems into the model. **Partner selection and orchestration**. Choosing providers, integrating them, and keeping the abstraction clean enough that one can be swapped without the rest moving — and that we can choose between them at runtime. **Customer reality**. Working closely with finance teams inside their actual close, their actual reconciliation, their actual disputes. **The bar**. You set the standard for whoever joins next, and you help choose them. We hire slowly and stay small on purpose. #### You'll probably recognise yourself - You've worked on payments, ledgers, or banking infrastructure, and you have opinions about double-entry, retries, and reconciling other people's data. - You are excited about how fintech will intersect with AI and want to build that future. - You've been on the wrong end of an idempotency bug and you design like it. - You've built a data model that survived three vendors and a market you didn't plan for or maintained one that didn't, and you know exactly where it broke. - You've integrated something documented one way and behaving another, and you found out before it cost anyone money. - You'd rather ship a narrow thing that reconciles than a general one that mostly does. #### Probably not for you if - You need the destination described before you'll start walking. Nobody here can hand you the spec, because the better version of this doesn't exist yet. - You want to be deep in one thing and served by the other. This role needs someone equally willing to debug a connection pool and to read a payment-message specification until they understand why a field exists. - You don't think AI will take a real role in finance. You don't have to be a maximalist. Scepticism is welcome and often correct and we encourage grounding. But the premise of the company is that this shift happens. #### How we work Very AI-pilled but anchored in reality. Small team, high trust, no ceremony. **Stack**: Python, FastAPI, Postgres, Next.js/TypeScript, Terraform, GCP/AWS

description: Qui sommes-nous ? Q ENERGY France est un acteur majeur du marché des énergies renouvelables en France. Autrefois affilié au groupe RES, l’entreprise œuvre depuis 27 ans dans le développement, la construction et l’exploitation de projets éoliens et photovoltaïques. Aujourd'hui également positionnée sur le marché du stockage d'énergie, Q ENERGY poursuit son expansion vers de nouveaux domaines afin de proposer des solutions intelligentes et complètes pour la production et la fourniture d’énergie durable en France. L'entreprise compte près de 300 collaborateur.rice.s et 6 agences sur le territoire ainsi qu'un siège social basé à Avignon. Q ENERGY France est une entreprise de la holding européenne Q ENERGY Solutions, créée en 2021 par Hanwha Solutions dans l'objectif de conduire à la prochaine génération de production d'énergie verte et flexible en Europe. Basée à Berlin, Q ENERGY Solutions est une société sœur de Q CELLS, fabricant de modules photovoltaïques reconnu à travers le monde. Les deux sociétés constituent la division Energie du groupe Hanwha Solutions, basé à Séoul. Vos missions : Rattaché.e au Responsable Asset Management and O&M, vous aurez pour objectifs d'analyser les performances des centrales éoliennes, photovoltaïques et de stockage et d'en garantir la fiabilité des données. Vos missions principales seront : Collaborer avec les gestionnaires d’actifs (Asset Managers) pour suivre et analyser les performances des parcs éoliens, photovoltaïques et des systèmes de stockage en exploitation. Garantir l’intégrité des données collectées, les analyser et les partager afin d’assurer une gestion efficace des tableaux de bord. Travailler avec les différents départements de Q ENERGY afin d’optimiser la rentabilité de nos projets éoliens, solaires et de stockage ainsi que la performance des centrales. Mettre en place des tableaux de bord automatisés à destination des parties prenantes. Administrer les bases de données et exploiter les outils MySQL et Power BI. Assurer le support dans la gestion quotidienne des données ainsi que dans la création des politiques et autorisations d’accès. Être responsable de l’historisation SCADA et des plateformes de supervision. Assurer la supervision des systèmes SCADA et des réseaux, réaliser les diagnostics SCADA, détecter les anomalies et les corriger pendant la phase d’exploitation. Être le référent technique pour toutes les questions liées au SCADA et à la gestion des installations éoliennes, photovoltaïques et de stockage en exploitation. Collaborer avec les équipes Développement, Achats et Construction afin d’améliorer les outils de suivi et de partager les bonnes pratiques. Participer à l’amélioration continue : fiabilité des installations, animation de groupes de travail. Assurer le suivi des obligations contractuelles du prestataire SCADA en phase d’exploitation. HSE : Contribution à la culture Santé, Sécurité et Environnement de l’entreprise via : Réalisation du travail dans le respect des mesures de prévention mises en place au sein de l’entreprise et reprises notamment dans le Document Unique, les Politiques Santé, Sécurité et Environnement, procédures, modes opératoires et guides Déclaration de tout événement ou situation pouvant représenter un danger pour les personnes y compris collègues et prestataires et/ou l’environnement Participation aux événements de formations et de sensibilisations traitant de ces thématiques Qualité : Respect et mise en œuvre de la politique d’entreprise et des procédures qualité Participation à la mise à jour des documents du système de management de la qualité Déclaration des non-conformités et participation à la mise en place d’actions correctives Participation aux actions et projets d’amélioration continue et de partage des savoirs Requirements Votre profil : De formation ingénieur généraliste, vous disposez de solides compétences techniques et aimez évoluer dans des environnements à la croisée de plusieurs expertises. Vous avez notamment de bonnes connaissances en automatisme, ainsi qu’en informatique et réseaux de communication. Des bases en électricité HT/BT vous permettent également de comprendre les principaux enjeux techniques liés aux installations. À l’aise dans les échanges, vous êtes reconnu.e pour vos qualités de communication, votre esprit d’équipe et votre capacité à travailler de manière autonome. Vous savez également prendre des décisions rapidement lorsque la situation l’exige. Un bon niveau d’anglais technique est attendu afin de pouvoir évoluer dans un environnement professionnel international. Une première expérience dans le secteur des énergies renouvelables serait un véritable atout, mais c’est avant tout votre curiosité, votre autonomie et votre envie de relever des défis techniques qui feront la différence ! Vous êtes donc mobile et appréciez le fait de pouvoir alterner entre travail au bureau et interventions directement sur le terrain. Benefits Comment faisons-nous la différence ? description: Wir bauen die Software, mit der WEG- und Mietverwaltungen ihren Alltag rechtssicher und ohne Medienbrüche organisieren, umfangreich und modern, aber erschwinglich, für das digitale Zeitalter der Immobilienwirtschaft. Die Immobilienverwaltung zählt zu den analogsten Branchen in Deutschland, genau das wollen wir ändern. Unser Team kombiniert Erfahrung aus dem Verwalteralltag mit dem IT-Know-how eines innovativen Tech-Unternehmens. Seit unserer Gründung 2020 sind wir aus der Praxis für die Praxis gewachsen. Wir sind ein Team von 26 Menschen in Brühl bei Köln, das Verantwortung ernst nimmt und Entscheidungen schnell trifft. Wir wachsen und mit uns die Anforderungen an unsere Infrastruktur über Marketing, Vertrieb und Customer Success hinweg. Dafür suchen wir keine Person, die HubSpot verwaltet, sondern jemanden, der sie baut: Strukturen, Automatisierungen und Tracking, die den gesamten Weg vom ersten Kontakt bis zur langfristigen Kundenbeziehung sauber abbilden. Du berichtest direkt an unsere CRO. Aufgaben Du übernimmst HubSpot als zentrale Infrastruktur für Marketing, Vertrieb und Customer Success und baust Strukturen, die mit unserem Wachstum mitskalieren. Du entwickelst Automatisierungen, die manuelle Arbeit aus unseren Teams herausnehmen, von Content-Automatisierung über Lead-Routing bis zu automatisierten Abläufen im Customer Success, etwa beim Onboarding neuer Kund:innen. Du baust mit n8n oder vergleichbaren Low-Code-Tools Workflows, die Systeme miteinander verbinden, die bisher nebeneinander laufen. Du setzt KI gezielt dort ein, wo sie echten Mehrwert bringt: bei Recherche, Optimierung, Datenanreicherung oder Content-Erstellung. Bei Bedarf baust du auch mal eine Landingpage in Webflow oder ein Tracking-Setup, das uns zeigt, was auf dem Weg zum Kunden tatsächlich funktioniert. Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing, Vertrieb und Customer Success zusammen und verstehst deren Prozesse gut genug, um sie in Systeme zu übersetzen, die im Alltag wirklich helfen. Qualifikation Gute bis sehr gute HubSpot-Kenntnisse: Du hast bereits Strukturen aufgebaut, nicht nur gepflegt, und weißt, wie Workflows, Properties und Automatisierungen zusammenspielen. Fortgeschrittene Erfahrung mit Automatisierung über Low-Code- oder No-Code-Tools wie n8n. Echtes Interesse an KI und was sie im Business-Kontext leisten kann. Du musst kein Profi sein, aber du hast bereits ausprobiert, gelernt und weißt, wo KI wirklich hilft und wo nicht. Ein Systemblick: Du denkst in Prozessen über Teamgrenzen hinweg, nicht in einzelnen Tickets, hast das Gesamtsystem im Kopf und weißt, wie sich eine Änderung an einer Stelle an anderer Stelle auswirkt. Technikaffinität, die über HubSpot hinausgeht. Ein Tool wie Webflow schreckt dich nicht ab. Bock, in einem Startup mitzugestalten, statt in einem eingespielten Prozess zu verwalten. Wer zu uns passt Wir suchen niemanden, der schon alles kann. Wir suchen jemanden mit echtem Interesse an der Aufgabe. Jemanden, der Automatisierung und KI nicht nur kennt, sondern gerne selbst in die Hand nimmt. Wichtig ist, dass du KI oder Automatisierung bereits im Business-Kontext eingesetzt, nicht nur privat ausprobiert hast. Das kann jemand mit ersten Erfahrungen sein, der Lust hat, sich weiter reinzuarbeiten, oder jemand mit viel Erfahrung, der Bock auf die nächste Stufe hat. Senior oder Expertin musst du dafür nicht sein. Entscheidend ist, dass dir das Bauen selbst Spaß macht, nicht nur das Ergebnis. Was SCALARA bietet Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit unserem CRO und echte Verantwortung ab dem ersten Tag. Die Möglichkeit, eine Infrastruktur von Grund auf mitzugestalten, statt eine bestehende zu verwalten. Ein Tech-Unternehmen, das auf Innovation und KI setzt und in dem gute Ideen schnell umgesetzt werden. Arbeitskultur: Ein offenes, wertschätzendes Team von 26 Menschen in Brühl bei Köln, das eng zusammenarbeitet und mit Herzblut und Spaß bei der Sache ist. Flexibilität: Hybrides Arbeiten zwischen Büro in Brühl und Home-Office, remote Arbeiten auf Anfrage. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description: Notre mission ⚖️ Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe. Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence. Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée. Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance. Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales. Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction. Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début. Sujet de stage Doctrine développe des workflows dédiés aux professionnels du droit pour accélérer et améliorer la gestion de leurs dossiers. Parmi eux, Jobexit accompagne les avocats et juristes en droit social dans la simulation de ruptures du contrat de travail, notamment en calculant les indemnités de départ, les indemnités en cas de contentieux, le calendrier de sortie et les allocations chômage. Dans un litige, un salarié peut demander plusieurs choses à la fois : des salaires impayés, une indemnité de licenciement, des dommages et intérêts, etc. L'objectif du stage est de permettre à l'utilisateur de saisir et d'organiser toutes ces demandes dans l'application, pour mieux estimer les montants en jeu, préparer la négociation avec la partie adverse et générer automatiquement le récapitulatif final destiné au juge. Ceci peut inclure : Concevoir une interface pour ajouter, modifier et réordonner les demandes d'un dossier, chacune avec son montant, son unité de calcul et son ordre Modéliser les dépendances entre demandes (une demande qui ne s'applique que si une autre est refusée par exemple) Calculer et afficher les montants (du coût pour l’employeur au net empoché par le salarié), pour aider l'utilisateur à évaluer les risques Générer automatiquement un document de synthèse clair et structuré, prêt à être intégré dans les conclusions écrites de l'avocat Et d'autres fonctionnalités ! Le ou la stagiaire participera à la compréhension du besoin utilisateur autour de ces outils (en collaboration avec les équipes produit et les juristes) et à la définition des solutions techniques (en collaboration avec les équipes techniques). Il ou elle rejoindra l’équipe Jobexit et participera également au chapter web (regroupement de tous les développeurs fullstack de l’entreprise). Les à-côtés du poste 👁️ Le ou la stagiaire participera comme tous les ingénieurs à son chapter (réuni 2 fois par mois) dont le but est de : Partager des connaissances entre ses membres (amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques) Proposer des améliorations (nouveaux outils et processus) Aider ses membres en fonction de leurs besoins Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝 Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert. Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides. Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien. Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc. Nos valeurs 🤝 Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses. Liberty and responsibility : n ous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership. Knowledge is power : l 'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser. Tech Consulting on digitaalisen suunnittelun ja ohjelmistokehityksen yksikkö, jossa autamme asiakkaitamme kasvamaan yhdistämällä liiketoimintamuotoilun, teknologisen asiantuntemuksen ja modernin ohjelmistokehityksen. Uskomme yhteistyöhön, avoimuuteen ja siihen, että parhaat ratkaisut syntyvät, kun erilaiset ihmiset ja ideat kohtaavat. Asiakkainamme on yli 130 organisaatiota eri toimialoilta, kuten julkishallinnosta, finanssi- ja eläkesektorilta, energia-, logistiikka- ja valmistavasta teollisuudesta. Kehitämme arjen digitaalisia palveluja, joita todennäköisesti käytät itsekin - ja joilla on todellista vaikutusta ihmisten arkeen ja yhteiskuntaan. Millaiset tehtävät sinua odottavat? Tässä roolissa yrittäjähenkisyys ja -asenne ovat keskiössä. Pääset muotoilemaan roolisi omien vahvuuksiesi mukaan osana tiimiämme - painopisteesi voi olla esimerkiksi myynnin tukemisessa, ratkaisujen määrittelyssä, teknisessä suunnittelussa, backlogien jalostamisessa tai toimintamallien kehittämisessä. Tehtäviä jaetaan joustavasti osaamisen mukaan, ja toivomme sinulta rohkeutta tuoda uusia näkökulmia myös asiakastyöhön. Autat asiakkaita siirtymään kohti pitkäjänteistä ja ketterää tuotekehitystä perinteisten, vaiheistettujen mallien sijaan. description: ### About Super44 We’re building the agentic copilot for local businesses. If you love your local coffee shop, book store, restaurant, boutique, or just good old off-license, this is your chance to help them not just survive, but actually thrive. We’re two repeat operators obsessed with building a “super-powered” sidekick for small business owners that orchestrates their tools and monitors their data to not only automate existing tasks, but change them and even come up with entirely new ones: **let ordinary people create extraordinary outcomes**. (alternatively: "Imagine Tony Stark's suit, just anyone gets to use one. Superpowers without the capes." We've just raised our pre-seed round, hired a founding engineer and now we’re now looking for **two founding engineers** to make the team 5 in total. ### The role As a Founding Engineer at Super44 you will: Ship end-to-end: napkin sketch → prototype → live with real merchants in half a day. - Build multi-agent, multi-model, multimodal systems that feel like magic and don’t break. - Jump across the stack: product, backend, AI agents, data pipelines and infra. - Working with rich business data, smart context management, and combining APIs and datasets to provide insights that drive real action (e.g. “boost revenue by 5% through smart pricing”). - Co-create our engineering culture: tech stack, tooling, quality bar, and how we ship. This is not a “feature team” role. You’ll be building core product and company, side by side with us. ### You might be a fit if… - You’re **high-horsepower** – you think from first principles, learn fast and like hard problems. - You’ve **built real things** end-to-end before, ideally in your own project or an early-stage startup. - You can go **full-stack** (or close): backend, some frontend, AI/automation – whatever it takes to ship. - You love **vibe coding** and rapid iteration, but still know when real engineering rigor matters. - You’re **energized by ambiguity** and the “no playbook yet” phase. - You’re up for working **really hard on something that matters**, with people you genuinely like. - You want a **tight-knit crew** where every team member really matters ### What we offer - **Day 0 impact**: Be #2/#3 employee of a startup with the ambition to become the operating system for millions of local business around the world - **Competitive salary *and* competitive equity** – we don’t want anyone joining us to choose between the two. Location: **Cologne–Bonn** region, building together in person. We have Superhouse, a hackerhouse overlooking the Rhein if you need accommodation. ### How we work We’re in full builder mode: working all the time we reasonably can, but focused on sustainable intensity. We like to: - Cut to the chase and always assume good intent. - Have strong opinions loosely held - Push each other to new heights and offer support along the way If this sounds like you, send us a short note about something you’ve built that you’re proud of (including links/github if you can). We’d love to meet you.

description: **Who we are** At Domino, we build solutions that help the largest, highly regulated organizations adopt AI to accelerate mission-critical use cases. Our platform integrates a streamlined model and app development environment, advanced model, agent, and app hosting capabilities, and novel governance capabilities providing regulator-ready AI at scale. Our customers — like Johnson & Johnson, GSK, Bristol Myers, UBS, FINRA and the US Navy — are using our software to solve some of the most important challenges in the world, such as developing new medicines, securing our financial markets, or protecting our country. Backed by Sequoia Capital, Coatue Management, NVIDIA, Snowflake and other leading investors, we have been in business for over a decade but are still a small team operating with the spirit of a startup. In the world of AI today, we believe that the future is still being invented — and we want to be the ones building it. For more information, visit [www.domino.ai](http://www.domino.ai) **What we are building** The Customer Engineering Solutions Team at Domino is the primary delivery engine that sits inside the walls of the world’s most regulated and demanding organizations, including Fortune 100 pharmaceutical and life sciences leaders. A Forward Deployed Engineer is a software engineer with solutions instincts, embedded in a customer's environment, building AI workflows on Domino that the customer couldn't have built as fast, or as well, without you. We write production code, ship it inside the customer's environment, and stay until Domino is fundamentally part of how they work. In the Life Sciences vertical, we build and deploy production-grade AI solutions that solve real, high-impact use cases, ranging from specialized AI inferencing workflows, custom cloud and data integrations, and interactive applications, to frontier solutions around Statistical Computing Environments (SCE), clinical CRM, etc. Our work provides the ultimate proof point that Domino is a comprehensive AI business solutions platform. **What your impact will be** In your first year, your impact will unfold across key milestones as you take ownership of strategic life sciences accounts: - **Day 0–30 (Onboard & Shadow):** You will be given the resources to master Domino platform mechanics and learn core user/admin functionalities. You will closely shadow the customer’s environment, pairing with a senior FDE to learn the client’s unique data, tooling stack, and commercial objectives. - **By Month 6 (Full Ownership):** You will step into full customer ownership across your engagements, executing independently against a prioritized backlog managed by your partner Engagement Manager (EM). You will build and deploy production-grade solutions across the entire MLOps lifecycle (development, deployment, and monitoring) while actively advising data science teams on Domino best practices. - **By Year 1 (Strategic Scale & Leverage):** You will lead and advise on key accounts, serving as a trusted advisor to technical and business stakeholders alike. You will author reusable playbooks, integration templates, and deployment guides for our shared knowledge base, measurably lifting the delivery speed of the entire FDE practice. Additionally, you will translate field intelligence into critical product feedback, routing platform signals to our SRE, Support, and Product teams to shape Domino’s roadmap. **What we look for in this role** - We are looking for a sharp, action-first engineer who possesses a unique blend of deep technical grit and customer empathy. - **Core Technical Stack:** Strong engineering roots with deep proficiency in Python (primary), alongside familiarity with SQL, R, and Bash. - **Cloud & Infrastructure:** Experience with Kubernetes and managed K8s solutions (such as EKS, AKS, or GKE), Docker, and cloud architecture (AWS, Azure, or GCP). You should be capable of troubleshooting networking, compute, and platform issues. - **AI & MLOps Experience:** A proven track record of delivering machine learning workflows, model deployment/monitoring, GPU workloads, and generative AI or agent frameworks. - **Regulated Environment Navigation:** Experience operating within, or consulting for, highly regulated or constrained environments. You can expertly navigate multi-factor constraints like strict compliance rules, data security hurdles, and infrastructure limits. - **Consultative Mindset:** Exceptional communication skills across both technical and business audiences. You are comfortable running structured discovery conversations, leading technical solutioning sessions, and translating messy customer requirements into buildable, tested solutions. - **Execution Style:** An "act fast, own it" mentality. You thrive in ambiguity, do not let blockers sit, and are comfortable making yourself productive inside an unfamiliar codebase quickly. **What we value** - We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply - We value a growth mindset. High-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and see the opportunities for success - We believe in individuals who seek truth and speak the truth and can be their whole selves at work - We value all of you that believe improving is always possible. At Domino, everything is a work in progress – we can do better at everything - We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company * * * #LI-Remote

You will closely shadow the customer’s environment, pairing with a senior FDE to learn the client’s unique data, tooling stack, and commercial objectives. - **By Month 6 (Full Ownership):** You will step into full customer ownership across your engagements, executing independently against a prioritized backlog managed by your partner Engagement Manager (EM). You will build and deploy production-grade solutions across the entire MLOps lifecycle (development, deployment, and monitoring) while actively advising data science teams on Domino best practices. - **By Year 1 (Strategic Scale & Leverage):** You will lead and advise on key accounts, serving as a trusted advisor to technical and business stakeholders alike. You will author reusable playbooks, integration templates, and deployment guides for our shared knowledge base, measurably lifting the delivery speed of the entire FDE practice. Additionally, you will translate field intelligence into critical product feedback, routing platform signals to our SRE, Support, and Product teams to shape Domino’s roadmap. **What we look for in this role** - We are looking for a sharp, action-first engineer who possesses a unique blend of deep technical grit and customer empathy. - **Core Technical Stack:** Strong engineering roots with deep proficiency in Python (primary), alongside familiarity with SQL, R, and Bash. - **Cloud & Infrastructure:** Experience with Kubernetes and managed K8s solutions (such as EKS, AKS, or GKE), Docker, and cloud architecture (AWS, Azure, or GCP). You should be capable of troubleshooting networking, compute, and platform issues. - **AI & MLOps Experience:** A proven track record of delivering machine learning workflows, model deployment/monitoring, GPU workloads, and generative AI or agent frameworks. - **Regulated Environment Navigation:** Experience operating within, or consulting for, highly regulated or constrained environments. You can expertly navigate multi-factor constraints like strict compliance rules, data security hurdles, and infrastructure limits. - **Consultative Mindset:** Exceptional communication skills across both technical and business audiences. You are comfortable running structured discovery conversations, leading technical solutioning sessions, and translating messy customer requirements into buildable, tested solutions. - **Execution Style:** An "act fast, own it" mentality. You thrive in ambiguity, do not let blockers sit, and are comfortable making yourself productive inside an unfamiliar codebase quickly. **What we value** - We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply - We value a growth mindset. High-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and see the opportunities for success - We believe in individuals who seek truth and speak the truth and can be their whole selves at work - We value all of you that believe improving is always possible. description: **About Us** Briidge.one is a custom AI and software transformation company helping established businesses turn fragmented operations, legacy systems and proprietary data into intelligent digital infrastructure. We work with businesses that have outgrown generic SaaS tools and need technology built around the way they actually operate. **Our work includes:** * Custom AI powered business systems * Internal operational platforms and dashboards * Client portals and visibility systems * AI reporting and query assistants * CRM, ERP, project management and workflow integrations * Legacy system modernization and digital transformation * Custom software infrastructure built around proprietary business data We typically work on high value transformation projects ranging from $20K–$100K+, working directly with founders, CEOs, partners and senior decision makers. We are now expanding our presence across high value industries including Private Equity, Law, Real Estate, Investment Firms, Professional Services and other established businesses. **The Role** We are looking for a Full Cycle Sales Executive / Business Development Partner who can own the entire sales process from first contact to closed deal. This is not a traditional SDR role where your responsibility ends after booking a meeting. You will be responsible for identifying the right accounts, initiating conversations, qualifying opportunities, running discovery calls, understanding business problems, positioning Briidge.one's solutions, preparing proposals, handling objections, negotiating with decision-makers, and ultimately closing the deal. You will work closely with the founding team but we are looking for someone who can eventually operate as the owner of their sales pipeline and revenue targets. If you can sell complex, high ticket B2B solutions and are comfortable speaking with CEOs, founders, partners and senior executives, this role is for you. **What You'll Own** 1. Prospecting & Account Research * Identify high value companies that have a genuine need for AI, automation, software modernization or digital transformation. * Research companies, their technology stack, business model, operational challenges and key decision makers. * Build targeted account and prospect lists using tools such as LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Apollo, Crunchbase and other intelligence platforms. * Identify the right stakeholders CEOs, Founders, Partners, COOs, CTOs, CIOs, Managing Directors and other senior decision makers. 2. Outbound Sales * Develop and execute highly personalized outbound campaigns across email, LinkedIn, calls, and other relevant channels. * Craft messaging around business outcomes, operational inefficiencies, revenue opportunities, cost reduction, and competitive advantage not generic software features. * Create multiple touchpoints and follow ups throughout the sales cycle. * Continuously test and improve messaging, targeting and outreach strategies. 3. Discovery & Qualification * Conduct discovery calls with qualified prospects. * Understand the prospect's current workflows, technology infrastructure, operational bottlenecks and business objectives. * Identify whether there is a genuine business case for custom software or AI transformation. * Qualify opportunities based on budget, authority, need, timing and strategic fit. * Translate complex business problems into clear opportunities for Briidge.one. 4. Solution Selling * Work with the founding/product team to develop the right solution for each qualified opportunity. * Clearly communicate how Briidge.one can solve the prospect's business problem. * Position custom software and AI as a business investment rather than simply a technology expense. * Build compelling business cases around ROI, efficiency, visibility, automation, scalability and revenue impact. 5. Proposal & Deal Management * Own the opportunity from discovery through proposal. * Coordinate with the internal team to develop proposals, scopes, and commercial structures. * Present proposals directly to decision makers. * Handle objections around pricing, implementation, risk, timelines and internal adoption. * Manage stakeholders throughout the buying process. * Keep opportunities moving forward and prevent deals from going cold. 6. Negotiation & Closing * Lead commercial conversations and negotiations. * Understand procurement and decision making processes within larger organizations. * Create urgency without using aggressive or transactional sales tactics. * Negotiate confidently while protecting deal value and margins. * Take ownership of getting qualified opportunities across the finish line. 7. CRM & Pipeline Management * Maintain a clean and accurate CRM. * Track every opportunity, interaction, next step and stakeholder. * Maintain accurate sales forecasts. * Build and manage your own pipeline. * Report weekly on pipeline value, conversion rates, sales activity, deal stages and revenue generated. **What We’re Looking For** * 3+ years of B2B sales experience, preferably selling software, technology, AI, digital transformation, consulting or other high ticket services. * Experience in managing a full sales cycle, from prospecting to closing. * Experience selling to founders, CEOs, C-suite executives, partners, or senior decision-makers. * Experience selling deals in the $20K+ range is strongly preferred. * Experience selling into Western markets. Particularly the US, UK, Europe, Canada or Australia. * Capability: The ability to understand complex custom software services and translate them into dead simple, compelling value propositions for non tech clients. **Why Join Us? (The Offer)** * High Ticket Sales- Work on projects typically ranging from $20K–$100K+, with the opportunity to earn meaningful commissions on revenue you generate. * Full Ownership- Own the entire sales cycle instead of being restricted to one stage of the funnel. * Direct Access to Founders- Work directly with the founding team and have a meaningful influence on Briidge.one's growth strategy. * Sell Something Custom- You're not selling another generic SaaS subscription. You're selling technology designed around a company's actual operations, data, and business objectives. * Total Flexibility: A remote first culture with completely flexible working hours. * A highly attractive commission structure tied directly to closed revenue, with additional earning potential through recurring retainers and account expansion. **Ideal Candidate** You're probably a great fit if you are someone who: * Can find your own opportunities. * Isn't afraid of cold outreach. * Enjoys talking to senior executives. * Can run a discovery call without a script. * Understands how businesses make purchasing decisions. * Can sell complex services without oversimplifying them. * Is comfortable with $20K–$100K+ conversations. * Can negotiate without immediately discounting. * Takes ownership when a deal gets stuck. * Measures success by revenue, not activity. * Wants to build something rather than simply work a sales job. If you know how to turn conversations into contracts, we want to hear from you.

description: Hi, I'm Robin. I'm building a company to design and manufacture industrial machinery (robots) to automate labor intensive processes in factories. We look for interesting opportunities for tasks in factories that can be automated, meet business owners that run those factories to learn as much about the process as possible and to turn them into future customers, and then we go back to our office to do our thing. Our thing is to design and build a machine from scratch. So that's brainstorming, CAD, software, assembling hardware, electronics, problem solving, more problem solving, and delivering the machine to customers. We have a 3D printer, lasercutter, plenty of other tools and a fairly large office/workspace in Amsterdam Sloterdijk. I like to design proper stuff, high quality. We want to build things that we are proud of. Things the customer will have as few issues with as possible. Things that will still work 10 years from now. We don't need to be icky about saving every possible cent. Of course there will be plenty of mistakes and redesigns, that's all part of the process, and that's okay. I'm funding this off of my savings, so I can't really pay you. But of course, you'd get your fair share of future earnings. Do you lose track of time in enthusiasm to build and develop stuff? Do you enjoy the mental game of finding the best solution for problems? If this sounds like something you'd enjoy being part of, send me a message! contact@zuttec.com, or let's just chat/meet up. I've got far more ideas than I have time for, so I'm sure there'll be plenty to do :) Cheers, Robin

description: Senior Process Engineer (Biomass Gasification) Company: Carbon Negative Power Location: Remote (with significant travel to project sites required) Job Type: Full-Time About Us At Carbon Negative Power, we partner with agricultural producers in the timber, plywood, and rice milling sectors to transform their biomass waste into a permanent economic advantage. We design, build, and operate custom on-site power plants that deliver reliable behind-the-meter baseload electricity at zero upfront cost to the producer. Our facilities convert organic residues into clean energy, biochar, and high-value carbon credits. We take on the engineering and capital risk so our partners can focus on their core business of agricultural production. The Role We are seeking an experienced Process Engineer with deep expertise in biomass gasification to lead the technical deployment of our carbon-negative energy facilities. This is a hybrid role. You will work remotely on process design and engineering while traveling to agricultural and industrial sites to supervise installations, oversee commissioning, and ensure operational excellence. Key Responsibilities Lead the process design and optimization for biomass gasification systems operating at core temperatures of 700°C. Travel to project sites to supervise the installation, integration, and commissioning of new power plants. Develop and refine mass and energy balances, Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs), and Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs) for facilities processing agricultural waste like rice husks, corn waste, and plywood residue. Serve as the primary technical lead on the ground during the build phase, ensuring construction aligns with strict engineering specifications and safety standards. Troubleshoot process bottlenecks during site startups and transition plants into smooth, continuous operation for behind-the-meter electricity generation. Collaborate closely with internal project teams and on-site agricultural partners to ensure seamless facility integration. About You Education: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a closely related technical field. Experience: Proven track record in process engineering with specific, hands-on experience in biomass gasification and thermal energy systems. Field Readiness: Highly comfortable transitioning from remote design work to hands-on site supervision. You must be willing to travel extensively to agricultural production sites for installations and commissioning. Technical Acumen: Strong proficiency in calculating mass and energy balances and developing technical diagrams for waste-to-energy pathways. Problem Solver: Ability to make critical engineering decisions on-site to keep construction and commissioning on schedule. Why Join Us? You will be at the forefront of decarbonizing heavy agriculture. This role offers the autonomy of remote work combined with the tangible satisfaction of building and commissioning physical infrastructure that eliminates energy costs for producers and removes carbon from the atmosphere. How to Apply Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your specific experience with biomass gasification and site installations. careers@carbonnegativepower.com

description: # **Forward Deployed Engineer** Sydney or Melbourne (Hybrid) ## **About Nash** Nash is building the digital logistics infrastructure that powers delivery for some of the world’s largest retailers, tech platforms, and delivery services. Our platform connects merchants, carriers, and customers through unified AI-driven logistics, helping enterprises like Walmart, Woolworths, 7-Eleven, and Coles orchestrate millions of deliveries every month. We’re now expanding our engineering presence in Australia and looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer who can ship code, solve real customer problems, and help shape how Nash scales across APAC. ## **The Role** This is hands-on engineering at the edge — not pre-sales, not implementation. You’ll build, deploy, and operate production software directly with customers while working closely with our global product and AI teams. You’ll be part of the foundational team defining how our Australia engineering office operates. Expect to move fast, own outcomes, and see your work drive real-world impact within weeks, not quarters. ## **What You’ll Do** • Build and deploy production systems used by top enterprise retailers • Work directly with customers’ engineering, ops, and leadership teams • Take new products from concept to live deployments • Design and extend core infrastructure underpinning global delivery orchestration • Partner with product and AI teams to influence direction across APAC • Debug real-world logistics workflows across fleets, APIs, and integrations ## **Who You Are** • 4 plus years building and shipping production software • Strong experience with APIs, backend systems, or platform integrations • Comfortable jumping between code, customer problems, and architecture decisions • Bias toward speed, iteration, and ownership • Clear communicator who can work directly with operators, CTOs, and execs • Motivated by building software that touches the physical world at scale ## **Why This Role** If you’ve wanted to join a high-velocity YC-backed startup redefining how logistics works worldwide — while getting to build and see your code operate inside real enterprise workflows — this is the one. Your work will touch millions of deliveries each month and help define Nash’s engineering footprint across APAC. **More about** [**Nash**](http://Nash.AI) ### **Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.** Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line. Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion. We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it. Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco. ### **What You’ll Love About Us** ✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career! ✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates ✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity ✅ Flexible paid time off ✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

description: Merista builds the physical AI workforce for food production. This is our founding team robotics hire, reporting to the CTO, owning the robot’s mind, and everything between intent and motion. Full-time and on-site in Barcelona. **The challenge** Food changes shape, sticks to tools, and behaves differently as containers empty. A successful movement can still produce an incorrect portion. A policy that works in a demonstration may struggle after hours of operation. That means the hard problems are the whole job: * How do we connect perception and manipulation when appearance alone doesn’t tell us how food will behave? * How do we control portion weight while meeting cycle-time requirements? * How do we detect a failed transfer and recover without stopping the line? * How do we collect demonstrations and production data that lead to measurable improvements? We expect robot learning to play an important role. You’ll help determine where it earns its place, how to evaluate it, and how it should work with sensing, control, and mechanical design. **What you’d own** You’ll lead technical choices across manipulation, learning, and control, working with perception and mechatronics engineers to define the interfaces. You’ll own the path from a policy’s output to reliable motion on the robot, including real-time execution, failure detection, and recovery. Your responsibility continues into deployment, where we find out which assumptions survive. * Execution and feedback control: trajectory generation, contact-rich manipulation, force control, and portion-weight feedback. You’ll connect policy outputs to real-time control, manage inference latency and timing, and define how the robot responds when an action cannot execute as intended. * Failure detection and recovery: detecting failed transfers and interrupted actions, bringing the robot to a safe state, and resuming work reliably. You’ll build automatic recovery where practical and give a remote operator the context and control needed to intervene. * Manipulation policies and learning: deciding what the policy outputs, how it is trained and evaluated, and where imitation learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, or conventional control earn their place with limited fleet data. * Data and evaluation: capturing useful demonstrations, failures, and recoveries, and building repeatable tests that show whether changes improve accuracy, speed, and reliability. **What you bring** * Hands-on experience building and running control software on real robot arms, including trajectory execution and feedback from sensors. You have taken manipulation from a demonstration into repeated, reliable operation. * Practical understanding of control-loop timing, latency, and fault handling. You can explain a failure you diagnosed on a physical robot, how you made it recover, and how you verified the fix. * Practical understanding of robot learning or related ML, including data quality, evaluation, and deployment. * Strong Python and enough systems understanding to debug across sensors, models, control, and hardware. * Evidence that you can take an ambiguous problem, design useful experiments, and learn from failures. * Interest in working closely with mechanical and mechatronics engineers. You don’t need prior food-industry experience. Show us something you built, what broke, and how you improved it. **About us** Most meals in the developed world pass through a food factory. The hardest and most repetitive manipulation tasks on the line still defeat machines, like portioning and assembling real food in small batches that frequently change. So people do them by hand in cold and wet rooms. Factories cannot keep those rooms staffed. Merista builds the physical AI workforce for food production: operated robots that take over these tasks. One robot rolls onto a factory floor without rebuilding the line. We deploy it and run it, and the factory pays for the work it does. We've already built and operated a multi-site robotic fleet for restaurants, dealt with production failures, field operations, remote recovery, hardware iteration, deployments and customers. Now we're starting again with a much more ambitious technical thesis. Our long-term vision is the self-driving food factory. The work today is one task at a time. **Why join at this stage** The core technical choices are still open. Your work will shape the data we collect, how we measure progress, and what we deploy. Our longer-term thesis is that useful factory deployments can create a compounding learning advantage: observe real failures, capture the right data, improve the system, and carry those improvements into the next deployment.
